hook.text: Short reads are like reading a book through a keyhole — long reads show entire pages at once.

buildup.text: PacBio HiFi reads span 15,000 bases with 99.9% accuracy — resolving repetitive regions that short reads scramble.

discovery.text: Oxford Nanopore reads DNA strands over 4 million bases long — entire genes, even centromeres, in a single read.

twist.text: The T2T Consortium used long reads to complete the human genome — filling gaps left by the original Human Genome Project.

climax.text: Long reads detect structural variants, methylation, and phasing simultaneously — one technology, multiple data layers.

punchline.text: Longer reads, clearer picture — long-read sequencing completes the genome.

quiz.question: What did the T2T Consortium achieve using long-read sequencing?
options: They sequenced the first animal genome ever
They completed the human genome by filling gaps the original Human Genome Project left unresolved
They reduced the cost of sequencing to under $1

details.summary: Long-read sequencing technologies from Pacific Biosciences and Oxford Nanopore read DNA fragments of 10,000 to over 100,000 bases, compared to 150 to 300 bases for short-read methods. This resolves repetitive regions, structural variants, and complex genomic rearrangements that short reads miss.

takeaways: Long reads span repetitive regions that short reads cannot resolve
They detect structural variants and complex rearrangements missed by short reads
Oxford Nanopore enables real-time sequencing in the field with portable devices

faq.question: What can long-read sequencing find that short reads cannot?
faq.answer: Long reads detect large structural variants including deletions, duplications, inversions, and translocations that short reads miss. They resolve tandem repeats, phase variants onto individual chromosomes, and directly detect DNA methylation without bisulfite conversion.

faq.question: Is long-read sequencing replacing short-read sequencing?
faq.answer: Not replacing but complementing. Short reads remain cheaper per base for standard applications like exome sequencing and RNA-seq. Long reads are essential for de novo genome assembly, structural variant detection, and resolving complex regions.
